title: Ouronet IPFS -> Arweave link map (Deploy/4_Arweave)
description: Consumed by REPL/tools/_arweave.py. Two modes, because the shape of an Arweave upload decides which one is even expressible. Run `python3 REPL/tools/_arweave.py --files` for the exact key list.

mode.description: manifest: the upload is an Arweave PATH MANIFEST, so the folder tree survives and only the gateway prefix changes. Three lines of JSON cover all 5,860 files. explicit: every file got its own independent Arweave transaction id, so every one must be named.

manifest.description: mode=manifest only. The Arweave base that REPLACES the IPFS gateway prefix, trailing slash included -- e.g. "https://arweave.net/<manifest-txid>/". Everything after the prefix (512x512/07_Bloodshed/4_Common/C_001.jpg) is carried across verbatim, so the uploaded tree must keep the same folder and file names.

explicit.description: mode=explicit only. OLD IPFS URL -> NEW Arweave URL, one entry per DISTINCT FILE. Keyed by old link rather than by nonce ON PURPOSE: Bloodshed's 12,928 rows share 272 images (mod 8/48/72/144), so a per-nonce keying would ask for the same string up to 56 times and offer 56 chances to disagree with itself. Every key must appear in `--files` output and every `--files` entry must appear here.

overrides.description: Valid in EITHER mode. OLD IPFS URL -> NEW Arweave URL, applied after the mode's own resolution. This is where the PADDING_ANOMALY files go: 132 Bloodshed rows ask for E_048.jpg / R_072.jpg / C_00144.jpg, three- and five-character names in a two- and three-character scheme (see _arweave.py PADDING_ANOMALY). If the Arweave tree names them E_48.jpg / R_72.jpg / C_144.jpg instead, name the three pairs here and manifest mode stays usable for everything else.
